meta.title: Three Kings Monument Chiang Mai — Visitor Guide, History & Legend
meta.description: A complete guide to the Three Kings Monument (Anusawari Sam Kasat) in Chiang Mai Old City: the founding of Chiang Mai by Kings Mengrai, Ramkhamhaeng and Ngam Muang, plus visiting info, photos and reviews.

about.label: — 02 · About the monument —
about.heading: About the Three Kings Monument
about.lead: A landmark at the heart of Chiang Mai Old City, honouring a great friendship and alliance in Lanna history.
about.paragraph1: The Three Kings Monument stands in an open square in front of the Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Centre (the former provincial hall), inside the old city walls. It marks the starting point of the famous Sunday Walking Street and is a must-see for every visitor.
about.paragraph2: The three bronze statues depict King Mengrai, the founder of Chiang Mai; King Ramkhamhaeng the Great of Sukhothai; and King Ngam Muang of Phayao. According to legend, the three were close friends and allies who together founded Chiang Mai in 1296.
about.quote: The three kings who founded Chiang Mai remind us of friendship, unity and the wisdom of good governance.

history.label: — 03 · History & legend —
history.heading: The history and legend of the Three Kings
history.intro: In 1296, King Mengrai chose this site together with King Ramkhamhaeng and King Ngam Muang to found 'Nopburi Si Nakhon Ping Chiang Mai'. The monument honours not only three great kings but also the friendship and alliance that bound the kingdoms of Lanna, Sukhothai and Phayao.

blocks.title: The founding of Chiang Mai
blocks.text: King Mengrai moved his capital from Wiang Kum Kam and founded Chiang Mai as the new capital of Lanna, advised by Ramkhamhaeng and Ngam Muang on the strategic location.

blocks.title: An alliance of three kingdoms
blocks.text: Lanna, Sukhothai and Phayao were friends and allies, supporting one another in diplomacy and defence. This relationship became the foundation of regional stability.

blocks.title: A living heritage
blocks.text: Chiang Mai flourished as the centre of Lanna and remains so today; the Three Kings Monument has become the city's central symbol.

legend.title: The legend of friendship
legend.text: It is told that the three kings were genuine close friends who consulted one another on all important matters, and it was this bond that led to the founding of Chiang Mai.

didYouKnow.title: Did you know?
didYouKnow.text: The current bronze statues were cast in 1984, replacing the original cement statues built in 1973–74.

kings.name: King Mengrai
kings.desc: Founder of Chiang Mai and the Lanna Kingdom
kings.story: King Mengrai founded the Lanna Kingdom and, with his two friends, chose this site to establish Chiang Mai as his capital, recognising it as a strategic and resource-rich location.

kings.name: King Ramkhamhaeng the Great
kings.desc: Inventor of the Thai script and father of Sukhothai
kings.story: King Ramkhamhaeng is credited with inventing the Thai script and promoting Buddhism. As a friend of Mengrai, he offered key advice in founding Chiang Mai.

kings.name: King Ngam Muang
kings.story: King Ngam Muang of Phayao was one of the three kings who founded Chiang Mai. Legend says the three were bound by a strong friendship and aided each other in times of war and hardship.

artistry.label: — 03.5 · Art & sculpture —
artistry.heading: The beauty of the bronze sculpture
artistry.intro: The Three Kings Monument blends historical narrative with the craftsmanship of northern Thai bronze casters.

items.title: Bronze casting
items.desc: The statues are cast in bronze by skilled artisans; the patinated surface is both beautiful and durable.

items.title: Detail and proportion
items.desc: Each king's face and attire are finely modelled, conveying the character of every ruler.

items.title: Setting in an open square
items.desc: The monument stands in a spacious open square, ideal to view and photograph from many angles.
